header.running_head: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Refuses to Accept Wealth Given to him

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) the Freed Slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ Refuses to Accept Wealth Given to him

Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) the freed slave of Rasulullaah ﷺ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "O Abu Raafi! What will be your condition when you become a poor man?" He replied, "Should I then not send some money forward (to the Aakhirah by giving Sadaqah since I will have nothing to give when I become poor)?" "Of course," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ, "but how much do you have?" Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) replied, "I have forty thousand Dirhams and I wish to give them all for the pleasure of Allaah." Rasulullaah ﷺ advised, "No (do not give it all away). Rather give only some away and keep some for yourself so that you may treat your son well."
Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) enquired, "Do they (our children) have rights due from us as we have rights due from them?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Certainly! The right that a father owes his child is to teach him the Book of Allaah, archery and swimming." A narration of Hadhrat Yazeed adds, "and to leave lawful wealth for him as inheritance." "When will I become a poor man?" asked Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA). "After my demise," came the reply.

Hadhrat Abu Sulaym says, "I saw Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) as a poor man sitting and saying, 'Who will be charitable towards an old and blind man? Who will be charitable towards a man whom Rasulullaah ﷺ had informed that he would become poor after Rasulullaah ﷺ's demise? Who will be charitable because the highest hand is Allaah's, the middle hand is that of the giver and the lowest hand is that of the beggar? Whoever begs unnecessarily will have an unsightly scar that will be seen on the Day of Qiyaamah. It is not permissible for a person to accept charity when he is wealthy or when he is in perfect health.' I then saw a man give him four Dirhams. When he returned one Dirham, the man said, 'O servant of Allaah! Please do not refuse my charity.' Hadhrat Abu Raafi (RA) explained, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ had forbidden me from hoarding extra wealth.' I then saw the time afterwards when he became so wealthy that I even saw the collectors of Ushr[^1] come to him. He then used to say, 'If only Abu Raafi had died when he was a poor man!' In exchange for their freedom, he would take from his slaves only that amount that he paid for them."[^2]
